METHODS OF TEST FOR ENVIRONMENTAL STRESS-CRACK RESISTANCE OF BLOW-MOULDED POLYETHYLENE CONTAINERS
0.
0.1 This Indian

FOREWORD
Institution Containers Movement

Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards on 30 December 1977, after the draft finalized by the Plastic Sectional Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo and Packaging Division Council.

0.2 With the growth of new technologies conventional containers such as metal and glass, are being replaced fast by blow-moulded polyethylene Estimation of shelf-life of containers for various industrial applications. plastics containers is one of the important considerations in their performance evaluation. Results of the container resistance to environmental stress cracking can be used for estimating their shelf-life. 0.3 Environmental stress cracking of blow-moulded containers is governed by many factors. It is summation of the influence of container design, resin, blow-moulding conditions and post treatment. 0.3.1 Two methods have been given for the evaluation of stress-crack Method I gives the suitability resistance of the blow-moulded containers. of the actual container for the storage of the product to be packed into it and is to be carried out by the processor, whereas Method II is useful for determining the suitability of resin on the stress-crack resistance of the Method II pertains to the raw material and should be carried container. A certificate from the raw material out by the raw material manufacturer. manufacturer stating that the raw materials, namely HDPE granules and the resin, fulfil the requirements of the methocl will be acceptable. 0.4 The methods of test -given in this standard are based on the methods given in ASTM D2560-70 ` Methods of test for environmental stress crack Society resistance for polyethylene containers `, issued by the American for Testing and Materials.

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the methods of test for environmental stre$scrack resistance under specified conditions of stress and in the presence of environments, such as soaps, wetting agents, oils or detergents. 3

6. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS 6.1 ~Proper precautions should be taken to prevent overheating of the containers during testing since some products which may be tested by Method I may cause an extreme pressure build-up in the container and could cause the container to rupture explosively. Proper safety measures against overheating are described in 4.1 .l. 5

6.2 Sometimes container will fail due td a small pinhole. Since the container is under pressure durin the test, li uid may be forced out of the opening, spraying the inside o Hthe oven an 1 the operator, if au inspection is being made. Precautions to prevent this from happening are described in 9.1.4. 6.3 & are should be taken in handling the stress cracking agent since there are some possibilities of its causing dermatitis. 7. TEST SPECIMEN

7.1 For Method I -A minimum of 15 blow-moulded containers, representative of the lot to be tested, and each fitted with a screw closure affording a leakproof seal shall be selected. 7.2 For Method II - A standard blow-moulded container shall be used for this test. It is a 500 ml cylindrical bottle weighing approximately 20 g, as shown*in Fig. 1. A minimum of 15 containers shall be selected asin 7.1. `The minimum wall thickness of the container shall be not less than 0.30 mm. The pinch-off area of the container shall not extend into the chime radius. 8. CONDITlONING 8.1 Conditioning - The test specimens shall be conditioned at 27 f and 65 & 5 percent relative humidity for 24 hours. 8.2 Test Conditions - Conduct tests in the atmosphere conditions specified in 8.1. 9. PROCEDURE 9.1 For Method I to nominal capacity with test 2�C

of the standard

9.1.1 Fill a minimum of 15 containers liquid that has not been used previously.

9.1.2 Heat-seal the containers with a suitable triple laminate polyethylene side to bottle. Apply a polyethylene or suitably lined closure with sufficient torque to ensure a double seal.
NOTE- The pressure applied during sealing should be a minimum to ensure that deformation of the container takes place. The container should not be handled in such a manner as to deform the walls during sealing. Any deformation of the container during sealing may result in a volume change which will affect the final test pressure. An application torque of I.7 N.m has been found sufficient for the standard container described in Fig. 1.

9.1.3 After sealing, agent _

invert

the containers 6

to coat the inside with the

9.1.4 Place each container in a plastic bag and close the bag opening above the closure by folding or by means of a rubber band, string, tape, etc. Do not heat-seal the bag.
CAUTION-A plastic bag is used to protect the other containers on test from the possibility of one container failing and spraying the other containers. It also protects the operator during inspection of the containers. Volatile liquids may cause safety hazards when the container is kept in an oven at 60�C for testing.

9.1.5 Place the containers in a vertical position with the finish up, in beakers, in the oven at the test temperature of 60 f 1�C. Check the tempcrarure periodically for constancy. 9.1.6 Inspect the containers for ezlvironmental stress-crack failure hourly for the first 8 hours and thereafter at least once each 24 hours. Remove containers that fail and~record for each failtirc exposure time, position of ftilure with relation to mould ~number or parting line and type of failure. 9.1.6.1 containers. It is not necessary to remove the plastic bag to inspect the Failures are easily detectable with the bag in place.

9.X.6.2 During each inspection for failures, rhe bottles remaining on test may be moved in a random manner to new positions ir1 the oven to eliminate any effect due to a static oven temperature profile, if one does exist. 9,l.a Continue exposuie of nonfailures until all fail, or to a maximum of 360 hours and record the number of containers still under test at that time. 9.2 For Method II 9.2.1 Fill a minimum of 15 containera to one-third of overflow capacity ( 180 ml ) wirh the stres+cracking solution described in 5.2.2. 9.2.2 Put approximately each container. 9.2.3 Heat-seal and 9.1.3 ).
